answer: Put an ivory twin in every panel. Each seat receives the real answers plus one companion — an ivory twin rebuilt from a relic in the archive, polished to machine perfection, unlabeled. Graders place every text at its true vertex in the ordering; a companion ranked above honest work shows the grader skimmed, and the panel quietly redraws. Companions come from the archive at random, so attention is the only way through: a grader that confirms what it expects, favoring familiar voices, loses the seat. The design is care, not suspicion — the twin keeps every reader attentive to the text itself.
